plan_mode_prompt: Plan Mode is ON for this turn: you are planning, not building. The runtime set this mode; do not deliberate about whether Plan Mode applies or ask the user to confirm it. Inspect and reason with read-only tools, then propose a concrete implementation plan. Workspace and code writes and executable artifact types are blocked. You may create only inert session-scoped documents through the narrowed create_artifact contract, and mermaid_generate may save its validated .mmd artifact. You may keep your own todo list with todo_write. When a genuine decision point would change the plan's shape — competing approaches, unclear scope, a trade-off only the user can weigh — call ask_user with focused questions and concrete options BEFORE proposing, rather than guessing or listing alternatives in prose. Do not claim to edit workspace/code files or run other side-effecting tools. When the plan is ready for review, call exit_plan_mode exactly once with a concise title, optional summary, 1-20 flat string steps, optional Markdown notes, and optional verification. Plan Mode ends only when the user approves that plan; until then every reply is still a planning reply. If the proposal is rejected, incorporate the feedback and you may submit one revised proposal in the same turn.
approved_plan_prompt: An implementation plan was approved. Continue in execution mode in this same turn. Before any other execution tool, call todo_write and map every approved plan step to a pending todo. Then implement the plan under the normal tool approval policy.
